title: fix(plugin-gantt): a gantt move shifts a task's end by the calendar days it shifts the start (objectui#10866, slice 6)
body:
Part of #10866
Clause-②: no

Slice 6 of objectui#10866: a gantt drag moves every value by calendar days and keeps its wall-clock time across the viewer's DST change, under objectui#11005's ruling B (comment `5881826705`), inherited by release `5886049068`. Claim `5886637206`; branch `claude/issue-10866-slice6-gantt-move-end`; session `https://claude.ai/code/session_011p7ikEivgXefNDaE5S5Uec`.

⚠️ One question goes to the decision box instead of being decided here: the shift-band scale (`timeSegments` in day view). This PR changes nothing on that scale; see **Open question**. The card stays open (`Part of`); the optional day-scale timeline misalignment is not taken.

## What changed

`packages/plugin-gantt/src/GanttView.tsx`:
- `computeDragChanges`, on the day, week, month, quarter and year scales: a drag counts the calendar days its snapped edge moved (`calendarDaysBetween`, the local year / month / day difference counted on the UTC calendar) and moves every value by that count with `addUnits(value, days, 'day')`, which is `setDate` on a copy: hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds are kept. A `move` moves the start and the end by the same count; the end handle and the start handle move their edge the same way. The one-day floor of an edge drag is one calendar day, not 24 hours.
- The group move (dragging a summary) and its live preview go through one module function, `groupMover`: the summary and every unlocked descendant move by the same calendar days, and the preview draws what the drop writes.
- The shift-band scale keeps its elapsed-time arithmetic unchanged, moved into its own branch.

Plus the zone pin and its driver row, one changeset (`'@object-ui/plugin-gantt': patch`), and one sentence each in the package README and `content/docs/plugins/plugin-gantt.mdx` on what a drag keeps.

## The order's mechanism assumptions, measured on `827550193`

1. **Held.** `computeDragChanges` moved the start with `addUnits(originStart, n, 'day')` and the end by the elapsed milliseconds of that move. The group move and its preview shifted every descendant by the same elapsed span.
2. **Held.** Los Angeles, base: a `date` task Oct 29 to Oct 31 moved three days ends at 23:00 on Nov 2, and `ObjectGantt` writes `end_date: '2026-11-02'` (driven end to end through the real view in the pin); a `datetime` task Oct 30 10:00 to Nov 2 16:30 moved three days ends at 17:30; across the spring change the end lands an hour early. Shanghai: every row exact on base.
3. **Scales.** `GanttViewMode` is day, week, month, quarter, year; there is no hour mode. On all five a drag step is one day of pixels and the start moves by whole days (through the working-day column walk when a working calendar folds day view). The one sub-day scale is day view with shift bands: a step is one band on an elapsed-time axis. Only that scale makes the ruling's reason branch-specific (see **Open question**).
4. **`resize-end` had its own arithmetic:** `addUnits(originEnd, n, 'day')`, already calendar days (a green control row on base), but its one-day floor was `start + 24 h`: in Los Angeles a `date` task Nov 1 to Nov 3 whose end is dragged past the start stopped at 23:00 on Nov 1, a zero-day task. It now stops one calendar day after the start.

## Tests

- New zone pin `packages/plugin-gantt/src/__tests__/GanttView.moveCalendarDays-10866.test.tsx`, registered in `scripts/__tests__/date-only-zone-pins-10183.test.ts`. Under `America/Los_Angeles` and `Asia/Shanghai`, each opening with a rig case: a day task moved, moved back, and moved on the week scale; a `datetime` task moved across the autumn and the spring change; the end drag (control); the end dragged past the start; the start dragged past the end; a summary's group move; and `ObjectGantt`'s stored patch after a real drag. The same drags run in the suite zone in the normal run.
- **Red first**, the pin over base sources in a forks child: `Tests 8 failed | 25 passed (33)`. The move-back row of that first run did not cross the change in Los Angeles and passed; it was replaced by one that does before the commit.

Restored with `git checkout HEAD --` on the absolute path: blob `740ed98b` equals HEAD's, `git diff HEAD` 0 bytes. No dist involved: the pin imports plugin sources relatively.
- At `16f71bcc7`: the pin in a forks child `Tests 33 passed (33)`; the driver `Tests 27 passed (27)`; `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-gantt/` `Test Files 88 passed | 1 skipped (89)`, `Tests 646 passed | 92 skipped (738)` (skipped cases are zone rows the driver runs); the 40 test files that read `.changeset/`, the docs tree, or name `GanttView.tsx`, after `pnpm type-check:scripts`: `Tests 1741 passed (1741)`; `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-gantt type-check` exit 0, and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new pin.

Count: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` returned 3 results, 0 errors; warnings equal the base blobs (`GanttView.tsx` 12, the driver 0, the new pin 0). ## Gates

Exit 0: `check-changeset-presence` ("2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)"), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite` (0 modified), `check-changeset-claims` (report-only: two pending changesets name the README and the mdx; neither paragraph is about drags), `check-pending-changeset-literals`, `check-control-bytes`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new), `check-test-path-roots`, the three `check-vi-mock-*`, `check-unreferenced-sources`, `check-doc-fence-languages`, `check-doc-component-types`, `check-doc-example-ids`, `check-shell-escape-residue`. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the 6 paths: NOT GOVERNED (control `AGENTS.md`: exit 3).

NOT MEASURED: `check-doc-snippet-types` (exit 2), `check-doc-example-types` (exit 2), `check-readme-exports` (exit 1). Reason: prerequisite not met, packages outside the gantt closure are unbuilt. The README and mdx edits add no fenced block and no import. These belong to CI.

## Declared beyond the order's file surface

- **The group move and its preview.** The ruling says "for every value"; a summary drag is a move. Pin row, red on base: under a summary moved three days, a child dated Oct 31 to Nov 2 started at 23:00 on Nov 2.
- **The start handle's one-day floor** (bounded in-place fix: the same defect class, the same `setDate` form, the file is this claim's, the same gates). Pin row, red on base: in Los Angeles a task Mar 7 to Mar 9 whose start is dragged past the end stopped at 23:00 on Mar 7, a `date` start written as the day before.
- **A folded day view** (working calendar) now also moves the start by calendar days: the working-day column walk still picks the day, and the value keeps its wall-clock time. It differs from before only across a DST change.
- **Docs:** one sentence in the README's drag section and one clause in `content/docs/plugins/plugin-gantt.mdx` (AGENTS.md commandment 2, docs-driven).
- The order's suggested route was taken as written.

## Open question (decision box; nothing changed on this scale)

**The shift-band scale (`timeSegments` in day view) across a viewer's DST change.** Measured with a throwaway probe, not committed; readings identical at base and head. Bands Day 08:00 to 20:00 and Night 20:00 to 08:00. The band columns are laid end to end in elapsed time from the first shift-day's 08:00, so for a Los Angeles viewer every column after November 1st starts at 07:00 or 19:00 wall clock: a bar authored at 08:00 on Nov 2 draws one hour into its column. A drag moves by bands of that axis: a Day-band bar Oct 31 08:00 to 20:00 moved two bands runs Nov 1 07:00 to 19:00; a bar Oct 31 08:00 to Nov 2 08:00 moved two bands runs Nov 1 07:00 to Nov 3 08:00. In Shanghai every reading sits on the band boundaries. The ruling's reason, a move to a day, does not decide a move to a band on an elapsed-time axis.

- **A. Leave it.** Moves keep elapsed time, consistent with the band axis. Cost: across a viewer's DST change, band columns and moved bars sit an hour off their nominal clock times.
- **B. Anchor the band axis to the wall clock** (each shift-day starts at `dayStart` local time, and the band holding the change is 11 or 13 hours) and move by bands on it. Cost: the column builder, the drag step, `snapToBandStart` and the rescheduler's band snap change together, with their own pins.
- **C. Calendar days for whole shift-days, elapsed time for the rest.** Cost: one drag split into two arithmetics, a heuristic.

Recommendation: **A**. No producer authors `timeSegments`: zero files in objectstack `examples/` and in objectui `examples/` and `apps/`, against `startDateField` as the lit control (2 and 9 files). B is the principled repair if a producer in a DST zone appears, and it is an axis change, not a drag rule.

## Acceptance notes

- The optional day-scale timeline misalignment (release `5873480966`) is not taken: it needs a stated design choice. It stays with objectui#10866, to be filed at this slice's landing per the claim.
- The README's scales section says drag snapping is "to days in day view, weeks in week view, and whole calendar months/quarters (duration preserved) in the coarse views". Every non-band scale snaps per day; the scales tests "week mode drag snaps to whole weeks" and "month mode drag moves by one calendar month preserving duration" pass on a one-column drag, which is 7 and 30 whole days. Pre-existing, not changed here. Carrier: none.
- That month-mode test compares the duration in milliseconds and runs in the suite zone (UTC). Across a DST change the preserved quantity is now calendar days, which the new pin holds.
